Description: A distinct offering delivered to customers, composed of capabilities and features.
A priced package or tier of the product defining what customers get and pay.
A high-level ability the product provides, realised by one or more features.
A distinct piece of product functionality that delivers value to users.
A request or piece of feedback from a customer or user asking for new or changed functionality.
A customer or user issue raised with support, which may lead to a bug, feature request, or answer.
A short statement of a need from the user's perspective, with the value it brings.
A concrete unit of engineering work needed to deliver a story, feature, or fix; kind is implementation or spike (a time-boxed investigation to reduce uncertainty).
A defect where the system behaves differently from its expected behaviour.
A known shortcut or deficiency in code or design that should be addressed later.
A large body of work that groups related user stories and features.
A strategic effort spanning multiple epics toward a business objective.
A measurable objective, such as an OKR, that work is expected to advance.
A planned item on the product roadmap with a target timeframe.
A versioned delivery of software to users or environments.
A significant checkpoint or date marking progress toward a goal.
A fixed time-box during which a team commits to completing a set of work.
A testable statement about expected cause and effect that an experiment validates or refutes.
A controlled test, such as an A/B test, comparing variants to measure their effect on a metric.
A testable condition a story or feature must meet to be considered done.
A representative archetype of a target user with goals and behaviours.
A group of users or customers sharing attributes, used for targeting, analysis, or rollout.
A description of how an actor interacts with the system to achieve a goal.
The end-to-end sequence of steps a user takes to accomplish an outcome.
A rule that constrains or defines how the business operates within the system.
A documented need or condition the system must satisfy; kind is functional, non-functional (such as performance, availability, or scalability), or accessibility.
A recorded choice made by a person or group, with its context, rationale, and outcome; kind is general or architecture (ADR).
A fixed technical or business limitation that solutions must respect.
A belief taken as true for planning or design that has not been verified.
A potential event that could negatively affect delivery, quality, or operations.
A document describing the design of a system or feature; kind is design doc or RFC (a proposed change open for review and discussion).
An organisational rule governing how work, data, or systems must be handled.
An external legal or industry requirement the system must comply with.
A specific control implemented to satisfy a policy or regulation.
An approved, time-bound exception to a policy, control, or requirement, with its justification.
A core business concept or defined term in the shared vocabulary that the system models or reasons about.
A deployable unit of software that provides a set of capabilities over an interface.
A top-level software system composed of services, data stores, and interfaces.
A boundary within which a domain model and its language are consistent.
A business area the software addresses, such as billing or onboarding.
A logical building block or module within a service or application.
A reusable code package or external system that a component relies on; kind is internal library or third-party.
A defined interface through which software exposes capabilities to consumers.
A single addressable operation of an API, such as an HTTP route.
A formal agreement on the shape and behaviour of an interface between parties.
A message signalling that something happened, published for other parts to consume.
A message instructing a specific component to perform an action.
A messaging channel or topic that carries events or commands between producers and consumers.
A connection between the system and another system or third-party provider to exchange data or trigger actions.
The movement of data between components, systems, or stores.
A multi-step business or technical process executed across one or more components.
A model of the states an entity can be in and the transitions between them.
A version-controlled store of source code and related files.
A line of development within a repository.
A proposed set of code changes submitted for review and merge.
A recorded snapshot of changes in a repository.
A single file of source code or configuration in a repository.
A code construct defining a type with state and behaviour.
A named block of code that performs a specific operation.
A configurable value that changes application behaviour without code changes; kind is application setting or environment variable.
A runtime toggle that enables or disables functionality for some or all users.
A pointer to a secret, such as a key or password, held in a secrets manager.
The person or team responsible for reviewing and maintaining an area of code.
The structure definition of a data store, message, or payload.
A table in a relational database holding rows of a given structure.
A managed data store instance holding one or more schemas.
A single typed field within a database table.
A database structure that speeds up lookups on one or more columns.
A stored database query exposed as a virtual table.
Precompiled database logic executed on the database server.
A versioned script that changes the database structure or data.
A code-level representation of a business entity and its behaviour.
A data transfer object used to carry data between layers or services.
A fixed set of named values used by code or data.
An ETL or ELT process that moves and transforms data between stores.
The recorded origin and transformation history of a dataset or field.
A curated collection of data used for analytics, reporting, or machine learning.
A product analytics event recording a user action or state, with its properties.
A trained machine learning model, with its version, inputs, and outputs.
A report or visual display of metrics built from data sources.
A sensitivity label, such as PII or confidential, applied to data.
A distinct page, view, or screen state presented to the user in a web or mobile application; kind is page or modal (an overlay dialog for focused interaction).
A set of input fields that collects and submits user data.
A URL path or navigation route that maps to a screen.
A reusable visual element such as a button, table, or card.
A single input within a form, such as a text box or dropdown.
A rule that checks user input before it is accepted.
A wireframe or visual design representing an intended UI.
A named design value, such as a colour or spacing unit, from the design system.
A template for emails, SMS, or push notifications sent to users.
A translatable piece of UI text keyed for multiple languages.
A specific set of inputs, steps, and expected results that verify behaviour; kind is unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, or security.
A grouped collection of test cases run together.
A document defining the scope, approach, and schedule of testing.
A single execution of tests along with its results.
Prepared data or state used to run tests consistently.
A simulated dependency used to isolate the code under test.
A report showing how much code or how many requirements the tests exercise.
A deployment or test target such as dev, test, staging, or production.
A geographic cloud region or availability zone where resources run.
An instance of releasing a build to an environment.
An automated pipeline that builds, tests, and deploys code.
An infrastructure-as-code definition, such as a Terraform module, that provisions resources.
An output of a build ready for deployment; kind is binary, package, or container image.
A group of compute nodes managed together to run workloads.
A physical or virtual machine that runs software.
A provisioned cloud asset such as a storage bucket, function, or managed service.
A recoverable copy of data or system state, with its schedule, retention, and location.
A spending limit or allocation for cloud or operational costs, tracked against actual spend.
A network segment, DNS zone, or routing configuration connecting resources.
A component that distributes traffic across multiple instances.
A task that runs automatically on a schedule, such as a cron job.
A measurement tracked over time such as latency or error rate, emitted for observability.
A measurement tracked over time measuring the success of a product, feature, or process.
A notification triggered when a monitored condition crosses a threshold.
A configured check that observes the health or behaviour of a system.
A service level objective defining a reliability or performance target.
A service level agreement committing to a level of service, with consequences if missed.
Step-by-step operational instructions for handling a task or incident.
An unplanned disruption or degradation of a service.
A review of an incident documenting causes, impact, and follow-up actions.
A source of logs or traces emitted by a system for observability.
A named set of access rights assigned to users or services.
A specific right to perform an action on a resource.
A non-human identity used by a service or automation to authenticate.
A process by which users or systems are authenticated and authorised.
A potential attack or misuse scenario identified during threat modelling.
A known weakness in code, configuration, or dependencies that could be exploited.
A digital certificate used for encryption or identity verification.
A cryptographic key used to encrypt, decrypt, or sign data.
A tamper-evident record of who did what, when, on which resource.
A group of people responsible for a set of products, services, or work.
An individual such as a contributor, owner, or stakeholder; role describes their interest in or influence over the product.
An external company that supplies software, services, or infrastructure.
A commercial or legal agreement, such as a vendor contract, customer contract, or licence.
An organisation or individual that uses or pays for the product.
A customer's active enrolment in a pricing plan, with its term, status, and billing cycle.
An isolated customer account or partition in a multi-tenant system.
A record of the discussions, decisions, and actions from a meeting.
A follow-up task assigned to a person, arising from a meeting, decision, or postmortem.
A frequently asked question paired with its answer.
A document explaining how to accomplish a specific task.
A record of notable changes in a release or to a component, for users or internal audiences.
